utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-67-R77.4, in the matter of Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Seselj, are you hearing me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am hearing you in translation into the Serbian language, which is the only language that I understand. Here they have been inventing some new languages, Croatian, Bosnian, and what have you, but I only understand the Serbian language and I shall not allow my native tongue to be insulted by being designated B/C/S or some similar designations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, inasmuch as you do understand me, do I take it that you represent yourself in this initial appearance today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall be representing myself also in all coming cases regarding contempt. I have planned another seven cases, another seven proceedings to take place for contempt of court, in addition to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, notwithstanding that, you may have heard this before, I would begin by reminding you that you enjoy the right to remain silent at all times during these proceedings. And I will begin by briefly outlining the background to this case and the charge contained in the order in lieu of indictment issued against you, which for simplicity I would refer to as the indictment. On the 24th of July, 2009, in case number IT-03-67-R77.2, the Chamber found Mr. Seselj guilty of contempt for knowingly disclosing confidential information pertaining to three witnesses in a book and sentenced Mr. Seselj to a term of 15 months' imprisonment and ordered him to remove the book from his web site. During the course of the appellate proceedings in that case, the Chamber ordered Mr. Seselj to remove several confidential filings as well as the book from his web site. On the 3rd of August, 2010, the Office of the Prosecutor filed the urgent motion under Rule 77 concerning violation of orders of the Appeals Chamber before the Appeals Chamber, seeking, among other things, an order in lieu of indictment against Mr. Seselj for violating the orders of the Appeals Chamber to remove the confidential filings and the book from his web site. On the 15th of October, 2010, that part of the Office of the Prosecutor's motion was referred to this Chamber. On the 31st of January and the 17th of February, 2011, this Chamber issued orders in case number IT-03-67-R77.3 ordering Mr. Seselj to remove confidential material from his web site. On the 31st of January, 2011, this Chamber issued an order in case IT-02-54-Misc.4 also ordering Mr. Seselj to remove confidential items from his web site. On the 9th of May, 2011, this Chamber issued the confidential decision on failure to remove confidential information from the web site, noting that each of the filings and books that Mr. Seselj had been ordered to remove pursuant to the orders of this Chamber and the Appeals Chamber remained available on the web site and initiating contempt proceedings against him for knowingly and wilfully failing to comply with the Chamber's orders. The indictment was appended to that decision. Mr. Seselj, according to the indictment you're charged with one count of contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under Rule 77(A) and Rule 77(A)(ii) for knowingly and wilfully failing to comply with the Chamber's order to remove confidential information from the web site. At this point I would invite you, Mr. Seselj, to formally identify yourself by name and how otherwise you are known and identified.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Dr. Vojislav Seselj, university professor and the greatest enemy of the Tribunal at The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything else you wish to add by way of identification?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there are many things that I could state, for instance, that I'm the only indictee who managed to tear apart the ICTY, that the ICTY has lost all moral and professional credibility in the proceedings conducted against me. I could talk all day long about the results and the successes of my nine-year-long struggle with the Tribunal in The Hague. I'm not sure that you are prepared to listen to all that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, again, I would -- would you be so kind as to read out Articles 20 and 21 of the Tribunal's Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. "Article 20: Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. 1. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. 2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or arrest warrant of the international tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the international tribunal. 3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instructs the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set a date for trial. 4. The hearing shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidences. Article 21: Rights of the accused. 1. All persons shall be equal before the international tribunal. 2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing subject to Article 22 of the Statute. 3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to the provisions of the present Statute. 4. In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality. (A) To be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and the charge of the cause against him. (B) To have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing. (C) To be tried without undue delay. (D) To be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing. To be informed if he does not have legal assistance of this right and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interests of justice so require and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it. (E) To examine or have examined the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him. (F) To have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal. (G) Not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Seselj, would you confirm the information that I have that you are in receipt of the indictment in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have received the indictment, but it was as far back as on the 12th of May. So I can see that this provision of the Statute is not being honoured, namely, that there should be no delays in my trial. It was -- it was on the 9th of May that the indictment was issued and it was submitted to me on the 12th of May, so that some two months have already elapsed in fact for this initial appearance of mine to only take place today. It was not scheduled, Mr. Hall, within a reasonable period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Your observations about delay are noted, Mr. Seselj. Now, you have the right to have the indictment read out in its entirety or you may choose to waive that right. Which do you prefer? What is your choice?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hall, I waive none of my rights. I insist that the indictment be read in extenso so that the public would see what it is that the Tribunal does because the public is quite aware of what it is that I am doing but it is not aware exactly what it is that the Tribunal is doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, bearing in mind the public interest in this matter, I am going to invite the Registrar to read out the public version of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Order in Lieu of an Indictment. "Vojislav Seselj born in 1954 in Sarajevo, Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and currently on trial before the Tribunal is charged with one count of contempt of the Tribunal pursuant to Rule 77(A) and 77(A)(ii) of the Rules as detailed below" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "Vojislav Seselj was ordered to remove various documents revealing confidential information the number a number of protected witnesses from case number IT-03-67 from his web site. The documents to be removed included three books authored by Vojislav Seselj and five filings made by him in case number IT-03-67-T, case number IT-03-67-R77.3 and IT-03-67-R77.2A. Vojislav Seselj acknowledged receipt of the Appeals Chamber's decision and the Chamber's orders to remove the confidential information from his web site on 5 January 2010 and 2 February 2011 and 21 February 2011 respectively. As of 9 May, the three books and the five filings remained available on Vojislav Seselj's web site. "The charges: "By his acts and omissions Vojislav Seselj committed contempt of the Tribunal punishable under this Tribunal's inherent powers and Rule 77(A) and 77(A)(ii) of the Rules for knowingly and wilfully interfering with the administration of justice by failing to remove from the web site confidential information in violation of orders of the Chamber."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seselj, the Rules provide that in proceedings --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters to finish the reading. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That under Rule 77(E) you would be called upon to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count of the indictment within ten days from the initial appearance. Under Rule 62(A)(iii) you may decide to immediately enter such a plea, and I also need to point out to you that should you fail to enter a plea at the initial appearance or any further appearance, the Trial Chamber under Rule 62(A)(iv) shall enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. So my question to you now is whether you are prepared to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hall, over these nine years I never was a factor who procrastinated proceedings against me. The proceedings were delayed either by the OTP or by the Trial Chamber. I am ready to enter a plea today and I say that I'm not guilty. At the same time, I challenge the right of the Tribunal at The Hague to conduct proceedings for contempt against me because contempt of court proceedings absolutely cannot be conducted for an indictee accused for the gravest crimes and not in the common-law system or in the continental system either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we have noted that you have entered a plea of not guilty. [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry, my microphone was off. To remind you that you are of course -- it is open to you, of course, to change your plea at any later stage of the proceedings. I return to a matter that I raised at the very beginning, and that is the question of legal representation. Is it the position that you are representing yourself? Would you be so good as to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I represent myself in this case as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, I am to remind you that self-representation is a qualified right under the Statute and the Rules provide that the Trial Chamber may, if it decides to do so in the interests of justice, instruct the Registrar to assign counsel to represent your interests. Now, again under the Rules, within ten days of this initial appearance you shall be provided in a language that you understand copies of the supporting material accompanying the indictment. On the 23rd of May you signed a proces-verbal indicating that you received 16 documents which were referred to in the Chamber's decision on failure to remove confidential information from the web site of the 9th of July, 2011. Additionally the Chamber hereby directs the Registry to provide the accused with its Rule 33(B) submission dated the 24th of June, 2011, as well as the annexes thereto within ten days from today. And I remind you, Mr. Seselj, that these materials are to remain confidential. I am also to remind you that preliminary motions under Rule 72(A) are to be filed within a ten-day period once you have received all of the supporting material in accordance with Rule 66. Mr. Seselj, are you in a position to today to say how long you would need to prepare your defence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm ready for the trial right away, but there is a problem, Mr. Hall. Whether the problem is solved or not, I'm prepared for the trial. You can schedule the trial as early as tomorrow. I sent a letter to the Registry on the 13th of June in which I informed them that in this third case against me for contempt of court I shall be representing myself and that I have a designated Master of Juridical Sciences, Dejan Mirovic as my legal advisor and Nemanja Sarovic, Bachelor of Jurisprudence, as my case manager. I requested the Registry to make it possible for my legal advisor and for my case manager to visit me immediately prior to my initial appearance and to be present today in the courtroom. I asked that the Registry to that effect pay their travelling expenses. You know that there is a decision by the Trial Chamber in the main case to the effect that the Registry shall finance my defence as of the day of the adoption of that decision to the tune of 50 per cent, which would normally be assigned to the defence of the accused who has an assigned defence counsel. I am contesting this decision of the Trial Chamber, but it has gone into effect and the Appellate Chamber has confirmed it. So that the minimum which was to be observed by the Registry was to pay the travelling expenses of my legal advisor and my case manager in order for them to visit me and to attend this initial appearance of mine here today in the courtroom. Yesterday I received a letter by Anna Osure, deputy of the Legal Assistance and Detention Affairs Unit and she said, in connection with my letter, that they have taken note of the fact that I shall be assisted by Mr. Mirovic and Mr. Sarovic, but none of the two gentlemen can be allowed access to confidential materials or privileged communication. But we are talking about my legal advisor from the main case, who does already have privileged communication with me and with whom I can establish daily telephone communications by safe telephone under number 9. So he already has privileged status in the main case. He also had such status in the two previous contempt of court cases and now he does not. Nemanja Sarovic has been my case manager for a long time also in the main proceedings conducted against me and also was that in both cases for contempt of court. They say that the Registry should make all the necessary basic checks with positive results, that yesterday on the 4th of July, in other words, they received the results of the basic checks and given specific issues that that raised, they were in no position to admit Mr. Mirovic as a privileged legal advisor until they received additional information. As far as Nemanja Sarovic is concerned, in connection with his status, they are still -- or namely, the President of the Tribunal has still not reached a decision pursuant to my appeal which I filed many months ago which has to do with his status, both in the main proceedings and in these contempt of court proceedings. In the end they say that I'm not entitled to financial resources, as financial assistance in the case, nor to the travelling expenses of my legal advisor. In addition, and I quote: "The Registry has not been satisfied that the initial appearance justifies deviation from the guide-lines of the Registry, especially in the absence of an order by the Trial Chamber for the attendance of your associates in the courtroom." Mr. Hall, in all civilised countries in the world it is the basic right of the accused to have at the initial appearance his legal advisor sitting at his side, whether as defence counsel or legal advisor; that is the fundamental right. And they are denying that right to me here. That is why I demand that the Trial Chamber that you are a member of immediately adopt a decision -- rule in this case and order the Registry to honour the privileged status of my legal advisor Dejan Mirovic and my case manager Nemanja Sarovic, and to make it possible for them to visit me within reasonable intervals of time for the duration of this process. I was never unreasonable in that sense and I was never visited by my advisors more often than once a month even in the main proceedings. And in these secondary proceedings perhaps it will be necessary for them to visit me once or twice during the entire case to assist me. The fact that I have decided to self-represent does not literally mean that I have to be alone. The fact that I am self-represented means that I am the first and the main -- the principal in my defence team but I have to have assistants. In some cases I have to have investigators, et cetera. In this case I probably should not be requiring any investigators. I had a problem in the last case of contempt of court. I brought ten witnesses. I asked the Registry to make it possible for me to prepare, to proof, those witnesses. This Registry prevented Mr. Mirovic and Mr. Sarovic from coming. I never prepared those witnesses at all, in any way. That is scandalous. No matter what the first-instance judgement may be in this process, it has to crumble before the Appellate Chamber when I tell them that I had not been given the chance to prepare my witnesses. These are things which actually discredit the Tribunal much more than I myself am able to discredit it in the courtroom. The Tribunal is discrediting itself the most, very often because of the cavalier attitude of the Registry. That is why I'm asking you as a Pre-Trial Judge and the Trial Chamber that you are a member of to make it possible for me in preparing the main trial to be able to communicate under privileged conditions with my legal advisor, with my case manager, and for the Tribunal to defray their travelling expenses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Of course the Trial Chamber is obliged to resolve such matters as remain unresolved and which are properly before it as distinct from those matters which are within the sole domain of the Registry and which have at the other end of the spectrum have not been resolved at the appellate level. So we've noted everything that you would have said today, Mr. Seselj. Are there any other matters you wish to raise before we take the adjournment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Hall, I would like to raise two issues. The first question has to do with the conditions of detention. I am placed on the floor of the Detention Unit where immediately after the -- his isolation was abolished, General Ratko Mladic also arrived. We socialise with him, we play chess, we spent time with him. However, the day before yesterday he had his repeated -- his further initial appearance and he refused any possibility of being represented by anyone from the list of the Registry and insisted on exclusively his two chosen Defence counsel who he trusts. And today the decision arrived that General Mladic should be moved from our floor to some other floor, whatever. It is not of consequence, within the same building. And this decision was motivated by the assumption that General Mladic, by socialising with me and by playing a lot of chess with me, came under my influence and that I actually influenced him to refuse all the attorneys on the list of the Tribunal and to insist only on Milos Saljic, an attorney-at-law from Belgrade, and Professor Alexander Mezyaev from Moscow who he both absolutely trusts. A certain Aleksandar Aleksic was tried to be imposed on him and some other people. It is true, I did say to him, You cannot absolutely have any confidence in anyone from the list of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Apart from the obvious fact that the arrangements at the Detention Centre are the responsibility of the governor of the Detention Centre, my question was I thought you were talking about that you had a complaint in terms of your own detention, if you would confine yourself to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was about to explain that, Mr. Hall. I personally am frustrated by such behaviour. I have some feeling of guilt that Mr. Mladic actually had to be moved on my account. That is what frustrates me and a frustrated person cannot adequately defend himself in court proceedings. I have to steer clear of any frustration. Secondly, as you are perhaps the only Judge with whom I shall be communicating as of this July until the summer recess of all of the Tribunal generally, I demand, this being the ninth year that I've been in detention, to be also granted annual leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is there anything else that you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will suffice and I am raising this question of my annual leave before you because probably I will not have any contacts with the Trial Chamber in the main case until the closing arguments. This was announced in their last decision, and who knows when that will be. So I am asking you to grant me annual leave and many indictees here have been granted annual leave, and that was actually the term used in decisions when they were granted provisional releases. Hadzihasanovic, the Muslim indictee, and Kubura, Kubura were -- these two gentlemen were given such leaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was going to ask for your assistance in explaining for the purposes of the record and for the -- and so that the Registry would fully understand what you're asking for, but did I understand you to mean what is otherwise referred to as provisional release? Is that what your application is?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm using it in that context and I invoke the fact that that expression was already used for provisional releases in the Hadzihasanovic/Kubura case. That decision also stated that they were being given annual leave for a month. Please bear in mind the fact that I have been here uninterruptedly for eight years and that this has violated all world standards as to the length of detention. Needless to say, there is also the fact that no one can guarantee for me. The only guarantee for me can be me, myself, but you have to deal with that problem. These rules say guarantees must be provided. There is no one who can provide guarantees for me, so there is a legal lacuna there. But you, as the judge in charge, must deal with that legal lacuna in keeping with general legal principles. What if someone is in no position to be provided any guarantees by anyone? I am not going to ask for guarantees from the treacherous pro-Western regime in Belgrade. I have no one else to turn to and I have been here for an accumulated period of eight years of detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Can you assist me in this regard, Mr. Seselj, should I interpret what you said, orally and without previous notice, to be your application for provisional release or do you intend to file a formal motion seeking provisional release? Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Mr. Hall, I understand fully. I will file no written application whatsoever. You know that in proceedings an oral application uttered in the courtroom has the same legal force as a written motion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this has been recorded and it's up to you to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I just want to be clear that what you said constitute your oral motion. So the Chamber is seized of it. Thank you, Mr. Seselj. And with that we would adjourn these proceedings to a date to be fixed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.40 p.m.
